newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus says float plans on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus says float plans on track.

text.p: SYDNEY, Aug 28 ()Reuter) - Australia's Optus Communiciatons Pty Ltd said on Wednesday that it still expects a public float by the end of 1996.
"The float's planned to occur this side of christmas and the prospectus is progressing to plan, but it is not done," said chief executive office Zygmunt Switkowski.
Switkowski said Optus would issue between 600 and 800 million shares in the float, which analysts expect to raise up A$1.5 billion.
He told reporters it was fair to say that revenue from its mobile phone business may exceed revenue from its long distance phone service by the end of 1996/97 year.

Revenue from Optus mobile phone business rose 55 percent to A$765.4 million in the year to June 30, 1996, while revenue from the long distance phone business rose 34 percent to A$810.8 million making it the company's largest business.

Switkowski said about 500 million shares will come from the planned sale by Mayne Nickless Ltd of its 25 percent, 100-200 million of new shares and the rest may come from existing insitutional investors.
"They (insitutional investors) have said they would sell down their existing stake and they are still reviewing that," Switkowski said.
He said Optus would raise between A$200-A$400 million from the issue of new equity.
"That band (A$200-A$400 million) is narrowing, and we just have to work out a final figure," he said.
Optus is 24.5 percent each owned by BellSouth Corp of the United States and Cable and Wireless Plc of Britain. Neither of these companies plan to dilute their stake.
The Australian Mutual Provident Society owns 10.3 percent of Optus, while National Mutual Holdings Ltd owns 6.1 percent and the AIDC Telecommunications Ltd fund owns 9.6 percent.
